related_questions.snippet: Almost 50 out of 100 people (almost 50%) with stage 1 liver cancer will survive their cancer for 4 years or more after they're diagnosed. Around 35 out of 100 people (around 35%) with stage 2 liver cancer will survive their cancer for 4 years or more after they're diagnosed.

related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of someone with HCC?

text_blocks.snippet: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) survival rates vary widely depending on factors like stage at diagnosis and treatment received, but generally, the prognosis is poor. Median survival can range from a few months to several years, with 5-year survival rates typically falling between 10% and 20%.
snippet_highlighted_words: Median survival can range from a few months to several years, with 5-year survival rates typically falling between 10% and 20%

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at HCC life expectancy:

list.title: 5-year survival rate:
list.snippet: The overall 5-year survival rate for HCC is around 21%.

list.title: Median survival:
list.snippet: Median survival following diagnosis is often around 6 to 20 months, according to a study in the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Factors affecting survival:
list.snippet: Factors like tumor stage, liver health, and treatment response significantly influence survival, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

list.title: Early detection:
list.snippet: Early diagnosis and treatment, like surgical resection, can lead to much higher survival rates, potentially above 70% at 5 years.

list.title: Advanced stages:
list.snippet: In contrast, advanced HCC stages may have survival rates below 20% at 5 years.

list.title: Stage A:
list.snippet: With treatment, 50-70% of patients with Stage A HCC may live at least 5 years.

list.title: Stage B:
list.snippet: Around half of patients with Stage B HCC may live more than 2 years with treatment.

list.title: Stage C:
list.snippet: With treatment, half of Stage C patients may live longer than 6-12 months.

list.title: Stage D:
list.snippet: Patients with Stage D HCC, due to advanced liver damage, may have a median survival of only around 4 months.

list.title: Curative treatments:
list.snippet: Liver transplantation and surgical resection can achieve 5-year survival rates above 50%.

list.title: Non-curative treatments:
list.snippet: Other treatments, like transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), may extend survival in advanced cases.
For advanced cases: When HCC is advanced, palliative care focuses on managing symptoms, improving quality of life, and providing supportive care.

list.title: Individualized prognosis:
list.snippet: It's crucial to remember that these are general statistics, and individual prognoses can vary significantly based on specific circumstances.

list.title: Consultation with a specialist:
list.snippet: If you have been diagnosed with HCC, consulting with a specialist is essential for understanding your specific prognosis and treatment options, according to the Canadian Cancer Society.
